title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and goal. This page is part of the continuation of the 'Longue Marche' (pp. 722–723). Grothendieck is building a canonical, base-point-free and S3-equivariant 'Abel–Jacobi' map from a thrice-punctured projective line to its generalized Jacobian. He needs it in families, over an arbitrary base S, including twisted forms. The aim (next page) is to apply this to the 'symmetric model' of a relative elliptic curve X/S given by a map S → M'_{1,1}.

Previous page (the split case). Let T^0 = G_m^{{0,1,∞}}/G_m(diag) ≅ G_m ⊗_Z M, where M = Z^3/Z·diag is the reduced permutation lattice of rank 2.
- Proposition: every (S3·T^0)-torsor over any base S has a unique rigidification, i.e. a unique S3-invariant section.
- Corollary (311): there is a unique S3-compatible morphism φ: U_{0,3,S} → T^0_S. Via the universal property of the generalized Jacobian it induces the identity on T^0.
- The NB identifies U_{0,3} with the line U_1 = {x_0 + x_1 + x_∞ = 0} inside the torus G_m^3/G_m.

This page, Corollary 3 (the twisted version).
- Data: Y/S is a Brauer–Severi scheme of relative dimension 1 (a form of P^1_S). S' ⊂ Y is a closed subscheme, étale of degree 3 over S. Put U = Y \ S'.
- (313): the generalized Jacobian (Rosenlicht's Jacobian with reduced modulus S', all degrees) sits in an exact sequence 1 → J^0_{U/S} → J^*_{U/S} → Z_S → 1, given by the degree map.
- The degree-0 part is a torus: J^0_{U/S} ≅ G_m ⊗_Z M(S'/S), with M(S'/S) = p_*(Z_{S'})/Z_S(diag).
- Equivalently J^0 ≅ R_{S'/S}(G_m)/G_m. This is a rank-2 twisted torus, obtained from the split lattice M by twisting with the S3-torsor attached to S'.
- (314): there is a unique morphism φ: U → J^0_{U/S} that commutes with Aut(S'/S) ≅ Aut_S(Y,S'). It is normalised by requiring that the composite J^0 → J^* → J^0 equals the identity, where Φ: J^* → J^0 is the map induced by φ through the universal property.
- This isomorphism of automorphism groups holds because PGL_2 acts simply 3-transitively on P^1, étale-locally.
- Thus φ is a canonical Albanese-type map with no base point: S3-symmetry replaces the choice of a base point.

Next page (the explicit formula). In the split case, with z the coordinate on P^1 \ {0,1,∞}:
- Ψ(z) = (−z, z−1, 1) mod scalars, which lands in the line x_0 + x_1 + x_∞ = 0.
- Ψ extends to P^1 ≅ the line in P^2, with 0 ↦ (0,1,−1), 1 ↦ (−1,0,1), ∞ ↦ (1,−1,0).

Where this is heading (inference). For an elliptic curve with 2 invertible, one takes Y = X/{±1}. S' is then the image of the three nontrivial 2-torsion points, which is étale of degree 3. The map φ becomes x ↦ (x − e_1 : x − e_2 : x − e_3) in a twisted torus. In other words, a canonical S3-symmetric Legendre-type coordinate.
errors: No real errors. I checked directly that Ψ(z) = (−z, z−1, 1) is S3-equivariant. Under z ↦ 1−z it becomes (z−1, −z, 1), which swaps x_0 and x_1. Under z ↦ 1/z it becomes, after rescaling by −z, (1, z−1, −z), which swaps x_0 and x_∞. So existence is explicit in the split case, and then everywhere by descent.

Uniqueness amounts to T^{0,S3} = 1. Invariance under the 3-cycle forces x = (1, λ, λ²) with λ³ = 1, and a transposition then forces λ = 1. So uniqueness holds over any base. The page uses this without stating it.

The page (and the previous one) asserts existence for arbitrary (S3·T^0)-torsors, which would need H^1(S3, T^0) = 0 or similar. In the case at hand existence follows from the explicit formula plus descent, so this is not a problem for Corollary 3.

ideas.what: The generalized Jacobian of a form of P^1 minus an étale degree-3 divisor S' is the twisted torus R_{S'/S}(G_m)/G_m = G_m ⊗ (p_*Z_{S'}/Z), extended by Z through the degree map.
ideas.modern_name: Rosenlicht generalized Jacobian with reduced modulus; Weil restriction torus modulo G_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenlicht, Serre (Groupes algébriques et corps de classes)
ideas.where_published: Not as such; the relative theory of generalized Jacobians is in SGA-era work and Serre's GACC

ideas.what: A unique Aut(S'/S)-equivariant, base-point-free Abel–Jacobi map U → J^0_{U/S}, normalised so that the induced endomorphism of J^0 is the identity; obtained by rigidifying an S3-torsor under the torus.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (symmetric) Albanese map; rigidification via vanishing of fixed points / H^1
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (this archive)

ideas.what: Explicit identification of P^1 \ {0,1,∞} with the line x_0 + x_1 + x_∞ = 0 in G_m^3/G_m, via z ↦ (−z, z−1, 1).
ideas.modern_name: Unit-equation line / S-unit line, a hyperplane in a torus

ideas.what: Intended application: X/{±1} for an elliptic curve with 2-torsion S' gives a canonical map to a twisted rank-2 torus over M'_{1,1}.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre form / symmetric model over the level-2 structure stack

missed.claim: A clean functorial formulation over an arbitrary base: for any form of P^1 with an étale triple of points, there is a canonical, base-point-free, automorphism-equivariant Abel–Jacobi map into the twisted torus R_{S'/S}G_m/G_m. It is presumably meant as the basis of a canonical 'symmetric model' of elliptic curves over M'_{1,1}, in the Teichmüller-tower / anabelian context of the Longue Marche. The mathematics is elementary and classical in substance, so this is mainly of documentary interest.
missed.quote: Il existe alors un unique morphisme φ : U → J°_{U/S} commutant à l'action de Aut(S'/S) ≃ Aut_S(Y,S')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it documents Grothendieck's method of rigidifying via symmetry instead of base points, which is relevant for descent of tangential-base-point constructions in the anabelian programme.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, neat but elementary construction: a canonical S3-equivariant map from a twisted thrice-punctured line to its generalized-Jacobian torus. It is classical in content; its only interest is as part of the unpublished Longue Marche programme on elliptic modular towers.
transcription_corrections: 'alors ont quoi[?]' is likely 'alors on a' (uncertain).
'M_4' may be a misreading of a subscript symbol (possibly M_∂ or similar); it denotes the lattice p_*(Z_{S'})/Z_S, which is locally isomorphic to Z^2.
'jac. compos[?]' is likely 'jac. généralisée, le composé'.
